newsitem.title: USA: Hancock closes ForesTree IV fund.
newsitem.headline: Hancock closes ForesTree IV fund.

text.p: The Hancock Timber Resource Group said it has closed its diversified ForesTree IV timberland investment fund with 13 institutional investors contributing a total of $128 million.

J.M. Huber Corp has contributed 115,000 acres of its timber holdings in Maine in exchange for participation in the fund. The Maine properties, which include softwood and hardwood used for a variety of products, are located in Somerset and Piscataquis counties.

The fund is also planning to acquire 11,000 acres of prime Douglas-fir region in Columbia County, Ore., part of a $350 million acquisition negotiated with Willamette Industries Inc and Hancock Timber earlier this year.

"We plan to round out the fund by investing in quality forestland in the South to provide our clients with optimal regional diversification," said Scott Jones, director of business development for the Hancock Timber Resource Group.

Hancock Timber Resource Group is a strategic alliance between John Hancock Financial Services and three regional forest management firms -- Wagner Forest Management Ltd, The Campbell Group Inc and Resource Management Service Inc.
